title: refactor: dev tooling bootstrap
desiredOutcome: Every later refactor commit is lint-gated: ruff (E9+F, py38) and vermin guard the 3.8 floor as dev/CI-only tools, and the house-style bans (walrus, typing, dataclasses, __future__) are AST-enforced in _output.py rather than remembered.

tasks.title: pyproject.toml with [tool.ruff]: py38, E9+F only, no formatter
tasks.description: Add a repo-root pyproject.toml carrying only [tool.ruff]: target-version py38, lint.select [E9,F]. No formatter: ruff format would churn thousands of aligned selftest labels for zero safety. Fix any true findings it surfaces (expected near zero given selftest coverage).

tasks.title: CI lint job: pinned ruff + vermin as the 3.8-floor gate
tasks.description: One new ubuntu job (~20s): pip install pinned ruff+vermin; ruff check plugins/audit tools; vermin -t=3.8 --no-tips --violations over scripts/ and hooks/. vermin is the actual floor gate: ruff parses with a modern grammar and target-version mostly steers UP-rules, so it will not reliably reject 3.9+ syntax.

tasks.title: House-style AST bans in _output.py, mutation-proven
tasks.description: Extend the existing AST lint machinery with bans version gates cannot catch: ast.NamedExpr (walrus is legal 3.8 but banned by style), from __future__, import typing, import dataclasses, across scripts/ and hooks/. Mutation-proven like the existing entry-guard cases: a fixture containing a walrus must be named; removing the ban must fail the case.

add: walrus/typing/dataclasses/__future__ bans fire on a named fixture and go green on the tree
